Recruiting - San Francisco and New York City

**About the Team**

The Recruiting Events program powers OpenAI’s top-of-funnel hiring engine through strategic, high-impact experiences that connect exceptional talent with our people, mission, culture, and work. From intimate dinners that build deep connections to conferences that expand our reach, we curate experiences that spark curiosity, showcase our work, and bring “Why OpenAI?” to life.

**About the Role**

We’re hiring a Program Manager to own a portfolio of recruiting events that supports OpenAI’s hiring priorities. Working closely with the Manager of Recruiting Events Strategy and Recruiting leaders, you’ll shape and scale experiences that attract, engage, and nurture priority talent, helping candidates envision a career at OpenAI.

You’ll translate hiring priorities into a thoughtful portfolio of event experiences and determine which events will most effectively engage the talent we need. You’ll help shape each experience’s goalsat, cross-functional participation, and success metrics, then lead initiatives from planning through delivery, follow-up coordination, and measurement. Your portfolio may evolve across business areas as hiring needs change.

You’ll own end-to-end program delivery and outcomes across your recruiting events portfolio, partnering with the Events team on large-scale production and logistics. You should be comfortable moving between strategic thinking and hands-on execution, with strong judgment, attention to detail, and the ability to influence without owning every aspect of delivery.

This role can be based in San Francisco or New York and requires being in the office three days per week. The role also requires extensive travel depending on the event schedule and workload, with occasional evening work as needed.

**In this role, you will:**

* Oversee programming across your recruiting events portfolio. Partner with Recruiting leads and hiring managers to prioritize monthly and quarterly event series based on hiring needs, target audiences, and partnerships. Apply the established program framework and lead initiatives end to end, adjusting plans as priorities evolve.
* Shape program content and event experiences. Work with recruiters to inform event strategy, audience and invitation plans, and speaker participation. Oversee the development of panels, product showcases, and other programming that reflects OpenAI’s recruiting brand and voice and supports each initiative’s objectives.
* Lead cross-functional partnerships. Align priorities, responsibilities, and timelines with Events, Workplace, Design, Communications, Marketing, and Procurement, resolving dependencies and guiding decisions that keep programs moving.
* Own program execution and post-event follow-up. Work closely with Recruiting Events coordinators to keep delivery on track across the portfolio. Ensure attendance and engagement information are captured, coordinate candidate follow-up with Recruiting partners, and establish clear ownership of next steps through program closeout.
* Manage portfolio performance and recommend improvements. Own KPI tracking and post-event reporting future programming.

**You might thrive in this role if you:**

* Have 6+ years of professional experience, with a background in recruiting programs or event program management.
* Have a track record of independently owning a portfolio of recurring event programs, with clear examples of how you improved execution, scaled programming, and measured outcomes.
* Make sound prioritization decisions and tradeoffs, anticipate risks, and adapt plans as hiring needs evolve.
* Build trusted relationships with Recruiting leads and partners across Global Events, Workplace, and other functions. You communicate clearly, influence decisions, and align teams around shared priorities and responsibilities.
* Bring creative judgment and attention to detail, with the ability to translate hiring needs into relevant audiences, compelling content, and thoughtful event experiences.
* Are a proactive, resourceful problem-solver who can resolve delivery challenges while identifying improvements that help an established program scale.
* Use data and qualitative feedback to evaluate performance, explain what is working, and make practical recommendations that strengthen recruiting outcomes.
* Are comfortable using Slack, Google Workspace, Notion, Airtable, and Jira to manage programs, maintain visibility, and support collaboration.

**We're hiring a Business Operations Analyst to run core operational areas that keep Longview functioning as we grow, and to make each one faster and more accurate.** Longview Philanthropy advises major donors and makes grants in AI safety and nuclear weapons policy. Our mission is to help the world navigate extreme risk and unlock an excellent future. Our two program teams are among the largest and most experienced in their respective fields. We directed over $75 million to high-impact organizations in 2025; 2026 will be substantially bigger.

Business Operations owns Longview's non-staff resources: AI tools, software, processes, contractors, equipment, and offices. Many of our processes were built when we were a much smaller organization. We’ve grown a lot, not just in headcount, but in offices, grantmaking, and fundraising too, and the routine work of keeping everything running has outgrown the time our current team can give it.

In this role:

* **You would run a set of operational areas day-to-day: the ops requests queue,** logistics for all-staff meetings and sprint planning, and support for our offices. Your manager sets priorities and reviews your work.
* **You would keep our knowledge easy to find.** You'd write step-by-step guides (SOPs) for recurring tasks and keep them current.
* **You would make each process better than you found it.** Business Operations is Longview's AI champion. When the same request keeps coming back, you'd build the fix: a self-serve answer, a template or an automation.

You'd report to Kaymin Martin-Burnett, our Business Operations Director, and work day-to-day with the Business Operations Associates on the team. By the end of your first three months, you should be reliably coordinating many central processes, e.g. software onboarding, office management tasks, and request triage; as well as at least one org-wide recurring process, such as the all-staff meeting, and each recurring task you own should have a clear SOP.

**You're likely a good fit if**

* **You've owned something real from start to finish**, such as a student organization's finances, a fellowship, or a process you improved at work, and you kept it accurate.
* **You want to build a career in operations** and like getting recurring work right.
* **You take the risks we work on seriously.** You don't need to be an AI safety or nuclear weapons policy expert. You understand why many people think advanced AI could cause catastrophic harm, believe that's worth working on, and can talk about it calmly and clearly.

===================

**Title:** Business Operations Analyst

**Reports to:** Kaymin Martin-Burnett, our Business Operations Director.

**Location:** We hire in the US and UK. We have a strong preference for candidates who can work from our New York or Washington DC office. We are also open to candidates who can work from our London office. You will be required to work from an office at least four days a week to build context and support your professional development.

**Start date:** ASAP, to be determined together with the successful applicant.

**Deadline:** We'll be reviewing applications on a rolling basis and encourage early applications.

**Compensation:**

US: $93,500 to $115,500 total compensation, which includes:

* $85,000 to $105,000 base salary
* 10% unconditional 401(k) contribution

UK: £69,850 to £86,350 total compensation, which includes:

* £63,500 to £78,500 base salary
* 10% employer pension contribution

See below for Longview's benefits, which include health insurance, a professional development budget, a well-being budget, and 36 days off per year, including holidays.

**Responsibilities**
====================

**Keep Longview's day-to-day operations reliable.**

* **Manage ops requests:** Stay on top of our ops requests queue, so every request gets an answer or lands with the right person. Turn repeat asks into self-serve answers or automations.
* **Coordinate org-wide meetings:** Run the logistics for all-staff meetings, team Q&A sessions (AMAs).

jobs.title: Account Manager, Enterprise, North America - AI Platform
jobs.description:
**About the job**

Help some of the world's largest enterprises get real value from AI. You'll grow a book of Whatfix's enterprise customers by bringing them new use cases, new applications and our AI-first products.

**Why this role**

* **Expansion-focused:** you won't carry renewals, so your time goes into growing accounts.
* **Existing & New AI products to sell:** into customers who already trust Whatfix.
* **Direct access to leadership:** work closely with our Co-Founder and CEO and our Global Head of Sales.
* **Uncapped incentives:** your upside grows with your accounts.

**About Whatfix**

Whatfix is an AI platform that helps enterprises get full value from the software and AI tools they invest in. We call this userization: technology should adapt to the user, not the other way round.

Our proprietary AI engine, ScreenSense, understands what a user is trying to do in an application and why, and delivers guidance, knowledge and automation in the flow of work. It powers Digital Adoption, Product Analytics and Mirror (simulation-based training), and our AI-first products: Seek, an AI assistant that acts across applications, and Mirror 2.0 for Gen AI role simulation.

We serve **700+ enterprise customers**, including 80+ Fortune 500 companies such as UPS Supply Chain Solutions.

We have raised **~$270M**, most recently a $125M Series E led by Warburg Pincus with SoftBank Vision Fund 2, and have been named a Leader in Digital Adoption Platform (DAP) reports by Gartner, Forrester, IDC and Everest Group for 5+ years running. We have four main offices in the US (San Jose), India (Bangalore and Gurgaon) and the UK (London), plus smaller offices in Germany, Singapore and Australia.

**The role**

As an Enterprise Account Manager, you will own a book of Whatfix's enterprise customers in your region and grow them.

Your quota comes entirely from expansion within those accounts: new business units, new applications and our newer AI products.

You will be based in our San Jose office and work closely with your customers in person, alongside our Customer Success, Solutions Consulting, Marketing and our product teams.

Our sales leadership, including our Co-Founder and CEO and our Global Head of Sales, is hands-on with the team, so expect direct mentorship and a short path from idea to decision.

**What you'll do**

* Own a portfolio of enterprise accounts end to end: expansion, cross-sell and account planning. This role does not carry renewals.
* Build relationships across each account, from CIOs and IT leaders to HR, L&D, CRM and procurement owners, so you are never single-threaded.
* Run structured discovery that gets to business impact, then build and quantify the ROI case for expansion.
* Find and open new business units and use cases inside your accounts.
* Position our AI products (Seek, Mirror 2.0 and the AI agents across our platform) credibly with senior buyers, and help customers shape how they roll out AI to their people.
* Use AI tools in your own work every day: account research, call prep, mutual action plans and follow-ups.
* Forecast accurately and keep the CRM current.
* Bring what you hear from customers back to Product and Marketing.

**What you'll bring**

* A track record of carrying and beating a quota in B2B SaaS, with real experience growing existing enterprise accounts through upsell and cross-sell.
* Experience in long, multi-stakeholder sales cycles with enterprise buyers, not only short transactional deals.
* Discovery and value-selling skills: you ask good questions, listen to the answers, and tie what you sell to the customer's business outcomes.
* The habit of building your own pipeline, including finding new teams and use cases inside accounts you already manage.
* AI fluency: you use AI tools daily in your own selling, and you can hold a confident, honest conversation with a CIO about how their organization adopts AI.
* Executive presence, preparation, and the honesty to say "I don't know, I'll find out" when that is the right answer.
* Coachability and curiosity. You seek feedback, act on it, and learn new products quickly.
* Comfort in a lean, fast-moving team where you will roll up your sleeves.

We hire for trajectory, not just pedigree. If you have moved from mid-market into enterprise, or from customer success or renewals into a commercial number, and you are on a steep learning curve, we want to hear from you.

**Where and how we work**

* **Location:** San Jose, CA. You will be based in our San Jose office.
* **Work model:** our teams work in the office 4 days a week to collaborate, build community and stay connected. US teams start their day early to overlap with other time zones, which keeps evenings free.
* **Travel:** up to 50% of your time, visiting customers across North America.

**Perks and benefits (US)**

* Uncapped incentives and an equity plan
* Mac shop: work with the latest tech
* Medical, dental and vision, with Whatfix covering 80% of premiums
* HSA: $1,000 individual / $2,000 family
* Monthly cell phone stipend and daily UberEats lunches
* Learning and development benefits, team and company outings
* Relocation and sponsorship available

**Our culture**

Customer First | Empathy | Transparency | Fail Fast & Scale Fast | No Hierarchies | Deep Dive & Innovate | Trust as the Foundation | Do It as You Own It

Whatfix is an Equal Opportunity Employer and E-Verify participant, complying with all EEO and ADA regulations.

jobs.description:
Summary
  
  
Imagine the contributions you can make at Apple. New insights have a way of becoming great products, services, and customer experiences very quickly. Passion and dedication are the keys to the accomplishments you can make here! We are seeking an experienced program manager to join the AIML Data Operations group. Our team directly contributes to the development of AIML algorithms across many of Apple's products, specifically in regards to Siri and Apple Intelligence. In this role, you will drive critical programs that enhance our operation to provide data at scale for engineering teams building robust AI features for millions of customers worldwide. You will spearhead business process re-engineering and organizational transformation initiatives, designing, implementing, and scaling intelligent, AI-augmented workflows that fundamentally modernize how our teams operate, scale, and deliver. You will develop various program elements, create and manage project plans, recruit participants internally and partner with various cross functional stakeholders.
  
  
Description
  
  
As a Program Manager within AIML Data Operations, you will lead cross-functional program management, define and implement policies and processes, and ensure clear communication with leadership. You will collaborate with DRIs and stakeholders to manage workflows, prioritize initiatives, and mitigate risks to drive program success. A core focus of this role is catalyzing operational and organizational transformation: you will evaluate existing operational systems, map complex end-to-end lifecycle journeys, and eliminate friction through structured process re-engineering. You will identify and champion high-impact opportunities where artificial intelligence—such as generative AI, LLM-based tooling, and automated agentic flows—can be integrated into day-to-day operations to modernize annotation pipelines, review cadences, and workforce orchestration. In doing so, you will guide teams through operating model shifts, establishing the alignment necessary for sustainable organizational adoption of AI-enabled workflows. This role involves defining policies that align with organizational goals, monitoring their effectiveness, and making data-driven decisions. Acting as the primary liaison, you will provide program updates, communicate risks, and support approvals with leadership. Successful candidates are highly organized, analytical, and proactive problem-solvers who excel at navigating challenges to deliver results.
  
  
Minimum Qualifications  
  
  

* Bachelors in Business Management, Engineering, Information Systems, Computer Science, Finance or related field; MBA or advanced degree preferred.
* 10+ years of experience managing large projects or programs including cross-functional initiatives across global teams.
* Proven track record in business process re-engineering (BPR), workflow redesign, and driving organizational transformation across complex, multi-tiered operations.
* Self-directed and proactive. You thrive in an ambiguous and fast-paced environment and bring a builder mindset to evolving team practices.
* Experience in working with cross-functional and Corporate teams (Legal, Privacy, Finance, and Engineering) to drive consensus, shepherd organizational alignment, and establish operating guidelines.
* Superb communication and presentation skills, both written and verbal. Can clearly articulate pointed questions to disambiguate, simplify and deliver actionable narrative to senior leadership.
* Aptitude for understanding and consolidating multiple points of view into an influential recommendation to move projects forward and rally teams behind transformative change.
* Excellent in teamwork and relationship building. Works to establish a collaborative relationship with other teams.
* Follows through on commitments exhibiting a high degree of personal ownership and accountability.
* Strategic thinker, continually looking for ways to increase productivity, leverage emerging technologies, guide organizational evolution, and decrease confusion for customers and operations teams.

  
  
  
Preferred Qualifications  
  
  

* Background in project/program management, organizational transformation, process optimization/Six Sigma, AI/automation enablement, operations, supply-chain, or business analytics.
* Hands-on experience identifying, developing, and deploying AI-driven workflows and automations (leveraging LLMs, intelligent document processing, generative AI tools, or modern orchestration platforms).
* Highly analytical, resourceful with data driven decision making and strong problem solving skills; adept at defining operational KPIs, workflow telemetry, and efficiency baselines to measure transformation impact.

  
  
  
At Apple, base pay is one part of our total compensation package and is determined within a range. This provides the opportunity to progress as you grow and develop within a role. The base pay range for this role is between $175,500 and $311,700, and your base pay will depend on your skills, qualifications, experience, and location.  
  
Apple employees also have the opportunity to become an Apple shareholder through participation in Apple’s discretionary employee stock programs. Apple employees are eligible for discretionary restricted stock unit awards, and can purchase Apple stock at a discount if voluntarily participating in Apple’s Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You’ll also receive benefits including: Comprehensive medical and dental coverage, retirement benefits, a range of discounted products and free services, and for formal education related to advancing your career at Apple, reimbursement for certain educational expenses — including tuition.
